text:
Mia (support): hi team — customer Chris from AcmeCorp is reporting intermittent 502s and timeouts hitting hosted inference (api.redwood.ai). They see a lot of "TLS handshake timeout" in their client logs after 18:40 UTC. Can we triage?

Chris (AcmeCorp): repro steps I can share: curl to our inference endpoint (region=us-west-2) -> some requests return 502, some hang then 504. Example: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED"`
Output: `* TLS handshake timeout` then eventually `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`

Mia (support): I've attached the customer's short tcpdump they captured (we asked for 30s capture). Looks like repeated ClientHello without ServerHello sometimes. Posting the small snippet: ```
00:00:01.123 IP client > api.redwood.ai: Flags [S], seq 0
00:00:01.456 IP client > api.redwood.ai: TLSv1.3 ClientHello
00:00:01.789 IP api.redwood.ai > client: RST
```

OpsMonitor (bot): new alert: gateway-5xx-spike us-west-2 18:38-18:46 UTC (p95 latency jump, 1200 errors)

Rashmi (eng-sre): thanks. quick checks: was there a cert rotation or infra deploy around that window? Any DNS changes? Also need the resolver used by the customer (their /etc/resolv.conf) if possible.

Kevin (eng-runtime): fyi we did a staged cert rotation for edge fleet in us-west earlier today at ~18:30 UTC (let me pull the deployment ID). It should have been seamless — rotation included chained certs and new intermediates. No config change to SNI.

Mia (support): Chris — can you paste `dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8` and `dig +short api.redwood.ai` (your default resolver)? Also, `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -timeout 5` output if available.

Chris (AcmeCorp): here's quick output: `dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8` -> `34.120.45.11` ; `dig +short api.redwood.ai` -> no answer (blank) sometimes, other times returns same IP. `openssl s_client` occasionally hangs and then: ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
139831234567168:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1543:SSL alert number 40
---
no peer certificate
---
```

Rashmi (eng-sre): that looks like resolver flapping (SERVFAILs) causing client to hit different edge IPs mid-flow while the cert rotation was happening. When resolver returns inconsistent answers, clients can attempt different endpoints which might have different TLS state. Do we have edge health for that IP?

Kevin (eng-runtime): pulling edge health for 34.120.45.11 -> `edge-health-check --ip 34.120.45.11` shows intermittent TLS backend errors around 18:35-18:44 (handshake timeouts) and a brief spike in worker OOMs on that node. We had autoscale bust earlier but not sure it explains handshake resets.

Mia (support): customer says only us-west-2 is affected. Chris — what's your client resolver (ISP)? Any DNS cache appliance?

Chris (AcmeCorp): our infra uses an internal resolver cluster (172.16.5.10) that forwards to 1.1.1.1. We saw SERVFAILs in our resolver logs matching the same window.

Rashmi (eng-sre): ok, plan: 1) Pause cert rotation rollouts to edge fleet for us-west until we confirm stable; 2) Ask infra (Kevin) to check the specific node and roll if necessary; 3) Recommend customer switch to 8.8.8.8 as a quick test and flush their resolver cache; 4) Request tcpdump + `dig +short` TTLs to see DNS TTL behavior.

Kevin (eng-runtime): I'm rolling affected node out of the pool now. Also checking if intermediate chain served by that node matches the CA bundle — sometimes missing intermediate -> handshake fail for some clients.

deploy-bot: rotation-job/us-west-edges/2026-03-15-1830 status: completed (partial), paused.

Mia (support): Chris can you try `dig +nocmd api.redwood.ai any +noall +answer` and `curl --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:34.120.45.11 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` (this fakes host header to that IP) and share results?

Chris (AcmeCorp): after switching to 8.8.8.8 and flushing cache:`dig +nocmd api.redwood.ai any +noall +answer` -> `api.redwood.ai. 44 IN A 34.120.45.11` ; `curl --resolve` -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` repeatedly for 10 requests. With default resolver still flapping -> reproduced 2/5 with errors.

Rashmi (eng-sre): that nails it — resolver flapping + a node with partial chain (or transient worker problems) created the bad intersection. Root cause: DNS resolver intermittency exposed a short window during cert rotation where an edge node responded with incomplete chain or was overloaded and reset TLS.

Kevin (eng-runtime): confirmed logs from node show `SSL_accept: certificate verify failed` and `missing intermediate certificate` for a subset of TLS handshakes around 18:33-18:40. I patched the node to serve the full chain and drained it. Also increased healthcheck sensitivity so we avoid routing while cert state is inconsistent.

Mia (support): mitigation steps we told customer: 1) flush local resolver cache and try 8.8.8.8 if possible; 2) if using an internal forwarder, ensure it isn't returning SERVFAILs (they can raise with their DNS team); 3) will re-run rollout with quick health checks after we confirm chain is correct; 4) we can add a temporary fallback IP / region for them.

Chris (AcmeCorp): after your patch and me flushing cache it's stable now, thanks. Can you confirm what you changed so I can update our runbook?

Kevin (eng-runtime): summary for runbook: when doing cert rotations, ensure full chain deployed to all edge nodes before higher TTL resolvers are hit; stagger rotations and increase healthcheck sensitivity; monitor for `SSL_accept` errors and treat them as fail-open for routing; coordinate with SRE to watch resolvers for SERVFAIL spikes. I'll add snippet to ops runbook and create a small check: `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -showcerts` should return full chain.

Rashmi (eng-sre): I'm opening an internal ticket (SRE-4287) to investigate why the node served incomplete chain — seems like packaging issue on one host during rotation. Also reach out to DNS provider for customer advising them about resolver flapping.

Mia (support): marking this thread resolved for now, will reopen if Chris sees recurrence. :white_check_mark:

Chris (AcmeCorp): thanks all, appreciated.
